1	# Rust Definition Language (RDL) Documentation
2	
3	RDL provides a Rust-like syntax for defining Windows types and APIs. It serves as an interface definition language for generating bindings and implementations for use with any language across the Windows ecosystem.
4	
5	## Quick Start
6	
7	```rust
8	#[winrt]
9	mod Contoso {
10	    mod Sprockets {
11	        // Define an interface
12	        interface ISprocket {
13	            fn GetStatus(&self) -> SprocketStatus;
14	            fn Spin(&self, speed: f32);
15	        }
16	
17	        // Define a struct
18	        struct Sprocket {
19	            TeethCount: u32,
20	            Diameter: f32,
21	        }
22	
23	        // Define an enum with explicit discriminants
24	        #[repr(i32)]
25	        enum SprocketStatus {
26	            Idle = 0,
27	            Spinning = 1,
28	            Locked = 2,
29	            Malfunctioning = 3,
30	        }
31	    }
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## Language Reference
36	
37	### Basic Syntax
38	
39	#### Comments
40	
41	```rust
42	// Single-line comments start with //
43	
44	/* Multi-line comments
45	   use C-style syntax */
46	```
47	
48	---
49	
50	### Attributes
51	
52	#### `#[winrt]`
53	
54	The `#[winrt]` attribute marks a module as containing WinRT types. When applied to a module, it enables WinRT-specific features like generic interfaces, generic delegates, and WinRT-style arrays.
55	
56	**Syntax:**
57	
58	```rust
59	#[winrt]
60	mod ModuleName {
61	    /* ... */
62	}
63	```
64	
65	**Example:**
66	
67	```rust
68	#[winrt]
69	mod Contoso {
70	    mod Sprockets {
71	        /* ... */
72	    }
73	}
74	```
75	
76	---
77	
78	#### `#[win32]`
79	
80	The `#[win32]` attribute marks a module as containing Win32 types. When applied to a module, it enables Win32-specific features like fixed-size arrays and union types.
81	
82	**Syntax:**
83	
84	```rust
85	#[win32]
86	mod ModuleName {
87	    /* ... */
88	}
89	```
90	
91	**Example:**
92	
93	```rust
94	#[win32]
95	mod Contoso {
96	    mod Sprockets {
97	        /* ... */
98	    }
99	}
100	```
101	
102	---
103	
104	### Type Definitions
105	
106	#### Modules (Namespaces)
107	
108	Modules provide a way to group types and APIs, simulating namespaces.
109	
110	**Syntax:**
111	
112	```rust
113	mod ModuleName {
114	    /* ... */
115	}
116	```
117	
118	Modules may be nested.
119	
120	**Example:**
121	
122	```rust
123	#[winrt]
124	mod Contoso {
125	    mod Sprockets {
126	        struct Sprocket {
127	            TeethCount: u32,
128	            Diameter: f32,
129	        }
130	
131	        #[repr(i32)]
132	        enum SprocketStatus {
133	            Idle = 0,
134	            Spinning = 1,
135	            Malfunctioning = 2,
136	        }
137	
138	        interface ISprocketFactory {
139	            fn CreateSprocket(&self, teeth: u32, diameter: f32) -> Sprocket;
140	            fn GetStatus(&self, s: Sprocket) -> SprocketStatus;
141	        }
142	    }
143	}
144	```
145	
146	---
147	
148	#### Enums
149	
150	Enums define a set of named constants.
151	
152	**Syntax:**
153	
154	```rust
155	#[repr(type)]
156	enum EnumName {
157	    Variant1 = value1,
158	    Variant2 = value2,
159	}
160	```
161	
162	The `#[repr(type)]` attribute specifies the underlying integer type. Supported types include `i8`, `u8`, `i16`, `u16`, `i32`, `u32`, `i64`, and `u64`.
163	
164	**Example:**
165	
166	```rust
167	#[repr(i32)]
168	enum SprocketStatus {
169	    Idle = 0,
170	    Spinning = 1,
171	    Locked = 2,
172	    Malfunctioning = 3,
173	}
174	```
175	
176	---
177	
178	#### Structs
179	
180	Structs define composite data types with named fields.
181	
182	**Syntax:**
183	
184	```rust
185	struct StructName {
186	    FieldName: Type,
187	    // ...
188	}
189	```
190	
191	**Example:**
192	
193	```rust
194	struct Sprocket {
195	    TeethCount: u32,
196	    Diameter: f32,
197	}
198	```
199	
200	**Fixed-Size Arrays (Win32):**
201	
202	In a `#[win32]`-annotated module, structs can include fixed-size arrays. This is useful for low-level data structures like buffers.
203	
204	**Syntax:**
205	
206	```rust
207	struct StructName {
208	    FieldName: [type; size],
209	    // ...
210	}
211	```
212	
213	**Example:**
214	
215	```rust
216	#[win32]
217	mod Contoso {
